title: Branch per row with CASE
description: Write a query that returns each product's `name` and a `price_tier` column: 'budget' for price under 20, 'mid' for 20 to 50, and 'premium' for anything above 50.
hints: CASE WHEN condition THEN value ... ELSE value END works like an if/elif/else chain, evaluated once per row - the conditions are checked in order, and the first one that matches wins.
Use CASE WHEN price < 20 THEN 'budget' WHEN price <= 50 THEN 'mid' ELSE 'premium' END AS price_tier, alongside name.
expected_behavior: Returns name and a computed price_tier per the three price bands.
solution:
SELECT name,
    CASE
        WHEN price < 20 THEN 'budget'
        WHEN price <= 50 THEN 'mid'
        ELSE 'premium'
    END AS price_tier
FROM products;
explanation: CASE evaluates its WHEN clauses top to bottom and stops at the first match, exactly like if/elif - ELSE is the catch-all for everything that didn't match an earlier condition.
